source_title: On the Discrete Logarithm Problem for Prime-Field Elliptic Curves

review_provenance.method: Direct inspection of the institutional accepted-manuscript PDF, with the mechanism, cost expression, assumptions, experiments, recovery, and conclusion checked against Sections 3-4.
review_provenance.boundary: This extract anchors what the paper states. It does not validate the unproved comparison T approximately T-prime or turn the reported toy experiments into cryptographic-scale evidence.

locator.value: Section 3; Section 3.2, p. 10 unnumbered T approximately T-prime assumption; Section 4

claims.paraphrase: The algorithm builds a factor base from random points R=uP+vQ, then replaces repeated decomposition and the final sparse linear-algebra step by one summation-polynomial system whose recovered point relation gives a linear congruence for the discrete logarithm.
claims.boundary: The claimed improvement is relative to the Petit et al. pipeline for fixed m and growing p, conditional on the unproved approximation T(E,m,V) approximately T-prime(E,m,V). The paper explicitly does not claim work below p^(1/2), reports only 11-22-bit experiments with m in {3,4,5}, and leaves the single-system cost poorly understood.
